newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro to offer new product line.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro to offer new product line.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc said Wednesday it unveiled Starfire (the Ultra Enterprise 10000 server), a new class of server for the data center that it said combines mainframe performance with "unprecedented scalability" and the benefits of network computing.
It said the Starfire system offers up to four times the performance at half the cost of International Business Machines Corp's CMOS mainframes and Hewlett-Packard Co's T series servers.

Sun Micro said the Starfire server enables customers to run the most demanding applications for data warehousing, decision support, on-line transaction processing and data analytics on a single scalable server.
It is a symmetric multiprocessing server scalable to 64 (250 MHz) UltraSPARC II processors, 64 gigabytes of memory with 64 I/O channels supporting over 20 terabytes of on-line storage.

Entry level configurations begin at 16 processors and scale to 64-way configurations. Pricing for an entry-level system starts around $870,000 (U.S.), which includes 16 processors and two gigabytes of memory. The system is available today with worldwide volume shipments in March 1997.
